title: Tech Note: Avoiding Problems Reading DOM XML Nodes
author: David Adams
featured_technology: DOM GET XML ELEMENT NAME/VALUE optional parameters
Custom ON ERR CALL error handling
DOM Count XML attributes / #document node special-casing

historical_commentary.text: This note is a foundational strategy guide for defensively navigating 4D's classic DOM XML tree, documenting four escalating techniques (testing the OK system variable, using optional name/value parameters on navigation commands, installing a custom ON ERR CALL handler, and writing a general node-validation routine) plus a special-case warning about DOM Count XML attributes crashing on the synthetic #document node. The specific DOM XML API is legacy relative to 4D's later native JSON support, but the defensive-programming principles it teaches — always validate before dereferencing, prefer safe optional-parameter APIs, and guard against undocumented edge cases in framework APIs — are timeless software engineering practices applicable well beyond XML.
related_updates: 4D added native JSON support and other modern data-interchange handling in later versions, making the classic DOM XML command set less central to new development
This note underlies the error-handling pattern (DOM_StartCustomErrorHandling/DOM_StopCustomErrorHandling/DOM_ReferenceIsValid) reused across several sibling 2006-2007 XML tech notes
